name: Scope
text: Adopt the dual-log system with a write-through checksum plus a background reconciliation worker now. Two fully independent logs run in parallel, each record carrying a checksum of its content and the last write’s logical clock. The reconciliation worker streams diffs in real time, blocking writes only when a proven mismatch is found—no central validator to fail, no silent corruption, and no blind spots. The trade-off is accepting a small latency hit on reconciled writes when splits occur.

name: Scriv
text: The write-through checksum plus background reconciliation still risks silent corruption if the reconciliation worker lags behind a fast split—user writes can race ahead before the diffs catch up. Instead, run two independent logs with a *write-through version vector* plus a *read-time conflict detector*: any read that hits a mismatch blocks until the logs reconcile, proving correctness before the user sees stale data. Settle it with a 24-hour load test injecting 10% write skew—if no corruption surfaces and p99 reads stay under 50ms, the version vector wins.
